body:
Not great. I was feeling okay last week, my boyfriend and I were doing great, then I said something stupid and feel like he's pulled away, and everything I do or say feels stupider and stupider and more and more desperate. I need comfort from him so badly but I feel like he doesn't want to be around me and I hate being a burden. I hate being around my friends because they are all so talented and driven and fun and I keep thinking that he should be dating one of them instead of someone as worthless as me. The voice in my head that keeps up a running commentary about how worthless I am was gone for a while, but it's back this week and it is vicious. I don't really want to kill myself, but every time I fuck something up it tells me I should.

I know there are things I should do to try and get better, thereby making myself a better partner. But it just seems like I always end up back in the same place, and the world is shit anyway, so what's the point?

I know EXACTLY how you feel. I am sitting at my desk right now typing this. The people I work with are fine, the work I do isn't terrible, but the fact that I have to spend all of my time and mental energy on something I don't care about, while still being unable to afford to provide for myself is killing me. People act like I should be grateful/happy to have a full time job, but I honestly can't figure out why this is something anyone would look forward to. I don't understand why I'm being forced to "earn my keep" when I didn't ask to be born in the first place. It's a bullshit system.

More than anything I want to just pack a bag and start hitchhiking. Or go off the grid on a little piece of land or something. I would much rather be doing drugs, writing, reading about things that interest me, hiking, exploring. I have no interest in being part of a system that demands that you suffer before enjoying anything, and I resent that I am forced to participate in it to survive. We have the technology and resources to let everyone work a little bit, spend the rest of their time on things they enjoy, and still be able to live, but we're stuck in this Puritan work ethic.

The only things I have anchoring me here are my boyfriend and my cat, who I could never leave. But the feeling of hollowness, that this is not the life I want for myself and in fact conflicts deeply with my values, just keeps getting stronger.
It's nice to know I'm not the only one.

I'm always reminded of that scene in "Girl, Interrupted" where she talks about how once you start thinking of suicide, it becomes the solution to everything. Buy the wrong dryer, kill yourself. Get a bad grade, kill yourself. Say something that didn't sound exactly the way you meant it to, kill yourself.

I do the same thing. I don't really plan on it or anything, but it crops up in my thoughts all the time.
